by: Claude (reviewer for the demo; the bank's data owner reviews for real)

value.reason: DATE_TIME is T24's YYMMDDHHMM audit stamp, the only time of day

changes.why: The proposal assumed YYYYMMDDHHMMSS; T24's DATE_TIME is a 10-character YYMMDDHHMM stamp. With the wrong format every transaction would have been dropped.

value.reason: FT transaction-type codes; TELLER is cash at a branch

changes.why: This bank's FUNDS.TRANSFER types OT and AC are entered through internet banking; TELLER records are cash.

value.reason: T24 has no device record; the sign-on terminal id is the nearest thing

changes.why: The proposal left Device unmapped. PROTOCOL.TERMINAL_ID identifies the terminal a user signed on from. There is no edge from a transfer to a sign-on, so device detectors stay off for this bank.

value.reason: PROTOCOL records whose APPLICATION is SIGN.ON

changes.why: F.PROTOCOL logs every activity; sign-ons are the rows with APPLICATION = SIGN.ON.
A TELLER record debits ACCOUNT.1 only when DR.CR.MARKER is DEBIT (a withdrawal).
A TELLER deposit credits ACCOUNT.1 when DR.CR.MARKER is CREDIT.
CALC/MANUAL.RISK.CLASS are AML risk classes, not a KYC score, and KYC.COMPLETE is YES/NO. Leaving it unmapped is better than a misleading number.

value.reason: posting restriction 25 is this bank's fraud block

changes.why: T24 has no case record; POSTING.RESTRICT 25 marks an account blocked for fraud.
